fields.label: Eyebrow (small label above the big heading)
Lead paragraph (subhead under the big heading)

runs.text: — a home block, a trailhead parking lot, or a new city for the weekend — the question stays the same: who nearby will trade a little honest curiosity?
Make low-stakes, in-person skill swaps feel natural —
when a moment lines up. Not a gig marketplace, not a course catalog — a calm path from “I wonder how that works” to “we tried it together.”
You pack questions the way you pack a jacket. The reflex to ask “could someone show me?” travels with you. Dabble balances

: repeat faces on familiar sidewalks, and the odd perfect afternoon — kayakers rigging boats in Golden, a stoop conversation about drywall in the Bronx, a fly-cast lesson on a borrowed riffle — without turning every hello into a transaction.

fields.label: Paragraph 2
fields.current: Dabble began on snow: a ski trip with my wife, a fly rod I did not quite know how to use, and the kindness of someone who slowed down long enough to show me the cast. It was not a lesson package — just humans passing a skill hand to hand.

pages.title: Community guidelines
pages.description: Who we welcome, honest skill claims, safe meetups, credits integrity, and how reporting works.

fields.label: SEO + social description
fields.current: Who we welcome, honest skill claims, safe meetups, credits integrity, and how reporting works — at the pace of a real conversation.

fields.label: Lead paragraph
fields.current: Dabble works because we walk the trail together — honestly, with care, and with room for beginners.

fields.label: Who we welcome (paragraph)
fields.current: Dabblers and curious visitors who treat each other with patience and dignity — across backgrounds, ages, and skill levels. The swap works best when everyone can breathe.

fields.label: Zero tolerance (paragraph)
fields.current: Harassment, hate, slurs, threats, intimidation, stalking, unwanted sexual attention, or coordinated pile-ons. People who break the trail rules don't stay on it.

runs.text: sharing what they have actually practiced — talent, skills, ideas, and knowledge — not on pretending to be something you are not.

fields.label: Bullet 1
fields.current: Say what you have done, how often, and in what setting.

fields.label: Bullet 2
fields.current: If you are not a certified instructor, do not imply licenses, insurance, union cards, or endorsements you do not have.

fields.label: Bullet 3
fields.current: If someone needs regulated work — electrical behind walls, medical decisions, legal advice — point them kindly toward a licensed professional.

runs.text: . The same checklist as the safety page (Master Plan §12.6):

fields.label: Bullet 1
fields.current: Meet in a public place the first time.

fields.label: Bullet 2
fields.current: Tell someone you trust where you are going and how long you expect to be.

fields.label: Bullet 3
fields.current: Keep the session short so expectations stay small; align with seed-phase credit norms when published.

fields.label: Bullet 4
fields.current: Stay in skilled-amateur territory; defer to licensed professionals for regulated work.

fields.label: Bullet 5
fields.current: Prefer in-app messaging until you are comfortable; keep phone numbers, email, and home addresses off your public profile.

fields.label: Bullet 6
fields.current: Leave if anything feels unsafe; report concerns to safety@dabble.it.com.

runs.text: For the broader safety model—including tiers and out-of-scope lists—visit

fields.label: Bullet 1
fields.current: No selling credits for cash or trading credits off-platform in ways that recreate a gig economy — the swap is the point.

fields.label: Bullet 2
fields.current: No ghost sessions or collusion to farm credits — if a meetup didn't happen, it didn't happen.

fields.label: Bullet 3
fields.current: Keep exchanges honest, in human scale, and aligned with the seed-phase credit story while it is in place.

fields.label: How to report (paragraph)
fields.current: Email safety@dabble.it.com with who was involved, when it happened, and what occurred — stick to facts you are comfortable sharing. In-product reporting will arrive later; email is the path for now.

fields.label: What happens next (paragraph)
fields.current: We triage, may pause or mute accounts while we review, and follow up with the Dabblers involved when it helps.

fields.label: 72-hour response promise (paragraph)
fields.current: During the seed phase we acknowledge substantive reports within 72 hours on business days. Some matters take longer to untangle; if so, we still send a first note inside that window so you are not left guessing.

sections.name: Four-tier framework
sections.blurb: Section heading, intro line, then four cards (Tier 1–4).

fields.label: Intro line
fields.current: Tiers and examples follow Master Plan §12.1–§12.4.

fields.label: Tier 1 — lead
fields.current: Short, informal moments — no scheduling pressure, no commitment beyond “nice to meet you.”

fields.label: Tier 1 — example 1
fields.current: Showing how to tie a bowline once while rigging a line at a public dock.

fields.label: Tier 1 — example 2
fields.current: Pointing out three edible mushrooms on an organized woods walk where the host group sets safety rules.

fields.label: Tier 1 — example 3
fields.current: Explaining one breaker reset step while a neighbor watches their own panel.

fields.label: Tier 2 — lead
fields.current: A planned exchange in a public or community setting, kept short.

fields.label: Tier 2 — example 1
fields.current: Forty minutes at a library table folding sourdough basics side by side.

fields.label: Tier 2 — example 2
fields.current: Helping someone swap brake pads at a farmers-market bike booth hosted by a local collective.

fields.label: Tier 2 — example 3
fields.current: Paddle-float practice at a staffed public beach where venue rules govern life jackets.

fields.label: Tier 3 — title
fields.current: Tier 3 — Continued practice with the same Dabbler

fields.label: Tier 3 — lead
fields.current: Follow-ups after a Tier 2 session, still bounded and still aligned with Dabble's no-cash, no-gigs posture.

fields.label: Tier 3 — example 1
fields.current: A second public session on the same topic because the first met both people’s boundaries.

fields.label: Tier 3 — example 2
fields.current: A small neighborhood circle (few people) hosted in a rented room or yard where everyone opts in.

fields.label: Tier 4 — lead
fields.current: Things Dabblers may choose privately, but the platform doesn't schedule or supervise.

fields.label: Tier 4 — example 1
fields.current: Solo work inside strangers’ private homes as a first meeting.

fields.label: Tier 4 — example 2
fields.current: Recurring dependent care, childcare without guardians present, or medical services.

fields.label: Tier 4 — example 3
fields.current: Anything that implies professional licensing, insurance, or background checks Dabble does not verify.

fields.label: Bullet 1
fields.current: Marketplace listings, cash tips solicited through profiles, urgency mechanics, leaderboards, or other product non-goals (payments, hustles, churn prompts).

fields.label: Bullet 2
fields.current: Sexual solicitation, dating, or escorting framed as “sessions.”

fields.label: Bullet 3
fields.current: Medical diagnosis, prescription advice, supervised withdrawal, or crisis mental-health treatment carried through Dabble chat.

fields.label: Bullet 4
fields.current: Weapons training aimed at harm, evasion of law, or instructions for illegal conduct wherever the participants are.
